---
title: "5. Within-sample diversity (alpha diversity)"
format:
  html:
    toc: false
---

*Examine diversity **within** each sample — alpha diversity — using the [Shannon index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diversity_index#Shannon_index){target="_blank"}, complementing the between-sample comparison of community composition in [step 4](tutorial-04-pcoa.qmd).*

### Calculate Shannon diversity per sample

We reuse `counts_filt`, the cluster-aggregated matrix from [step 4](tutorial-04-pcoa.qmd):

```r
shannon <- vegan::diversity(counts_filt, MARGIN = 2)
```

A higher Shannon index indicates greater within-sample diversity, reflecting both the number of clusters present and how evenly their abundances are distributed.

### Plot Shannon diversity by habitat

```r
par(mar = c(7, 4, 2, 1))
boxplot(shannon ~ habitat[ix], las = 2, xlab = "",
        ylab = "Shannon diversity",
        col = habitat_cols[levels(factor(habitat[ix]))])
```

The boxplots show how within-sample diversity varies within and between habitats.

This is distinct from the PCoA in step 4: two habitats can differ strongly in community composition while having similar levels of alpha diversity.
